reaper.notes: The Reapers: the mist's own uniform — the procession's hooded file and the ride's firing line. A tall hood cut to a short point, the face a dark slit with two pale eyes (X near, x far), the cowl to a point on the chest, the cloak A-lined to a torn hem. No hands at rest: `hand` is where the right hand rests inside the cloak. The stride is the hem's (a boot's toe at the reach, the planted boot under the risen hem). E `aim`: the rifle level out of the cloak under the eyes — the right hand on the grip under the action (W), the left far out under the fore-end, dark gloves, the long barrel (w).

lamplighter.notes: The Lamplighter on the ridge: the Reapers' cut to the texel, and a person in it — a face in the hood, the faded khaki scarf at the throat, the warm binding down the seam and round the hem, boots under it. The HOODED LANTERN hangs low from the RIGHT hand (one gold slit X, brass rim x; `light` is the slit's middle for the glow); the LEFT hand holds the sling at the chest. The C14 across the back: muzzle up past the right shoulder, butt out past the left hip, the sling over the chest.

stranger.notes: The raised-tongue stranger out of the bunker: olive coveralls zipped to a turned collar and belted in their own cloth, the leaf-green sash of an assigned career over the right shoulder to the left hip, hair short and parted, a face that has never seen weather, wire spectacles (w) with the right lens catching the light (W). Empty-handed; `hand` is the bare right hand. Arms and legs are the courier's own blocks (legs in coverall cloth).

tender.notes: The Flame Keepers' tender who stands the fed bowl: a hooded robe to the ground in the Keepers' red, a cord at the waist, the courier's hood shape; the TORCH held up in the RIGHT hand in every frame (haft V/v, the pitch-wrapped head n, the flame X heart / x edge above the hood; `light` is the flame's heart). The left arm hangs in its sleeve. idle2: the breath, and the flame's heart drawn up a row.

giant.notes: The far shape in the grey, COLOSSAL: 63 texels crown to sole (the old 156 world units at 2.5 a texel). One frame, facing the eye. Near-black body (O) with near-black plate faces (T, c, t); the dusk's rim (L) along the hull's and the crown's top edges, a dimmer rim (C) on the shoulder blocks and the knee housings; one red running light in the visor band — `eye` is its hot point x at (20, 5), X beside it at (21, 5) (pulse the pair between X and x as the old eye did). The head stands a texel right of the axis and its crown is cut on a slant; the right shoulder and knee housing sit a row lower.
